catalogue: Australian residential thermal, condensation, air-sealing and ventilation construction

objects.name: residential thermal and condensation-control system
objects.definition: The coordinated building-fabric, insulation, air, water and vapour-control layers plus ventilation and source-exhaust components used to manage heat flow, air leakage and moisture accumulation in a house.
functions: Coordinate heat, air and moisture control
Keep envelope layers continuous across junctions and openings
Provide deliberate drying, ventilation and exhaust paths

ncc_references.relationship: Coordinates condensation management with the selected energy-efficiency pathway without turning compliance outcomes into physical layers.

cad.pattern: Connected control layers and devices around the conditioned building envelope
cad.placement: Across roofs, ceilings, walls, floors, openings and service interfaces
cad.opening: Turns into or seals every documented opening and penetration
cad.load: Non-structural environmental-control system supported by building fabric

notes: Thermal performance, vapour permeance, airtightness and condensation risk are properties or analysis results; the drawable objects are the selected assemblies and components.

objects.name: residential thermal envelope assembly
objects.definition: The connected roof or ceiling, external wall, floor, glazing and door constructions that separate conditioned space from outdoor air, ground or an unconditioned adjoining space.
functions: Connect insulated opaque and glazed elements
Expose gaps and thermal bridges for coordination

cad.pattern: Closed set of connected envelope faces
cad.placement: At the boundary of conditioned spaces
cad.opening: Contains windows, doors, roof lights and sealed services
cad.load: Environmental boundary; structure remains in host assemblies

notes: A garage wall can be part of this boundary even when it is internal in plan; boundary status follows adjacent conditioned and unconditioned spaces.

objects.name: roof and ceiling thermal assembly
objects.definition: A roof or ceiling build-up containing the selected primary insulation, any continuous or reflective layer, required airspace, framing interruptions and coordinated service clearances.
functions: Limit heat transfer through the upper envelope
Coordinate thermal layers with roof-space moisture control

ncc_references.relationship: Physical insulation must be continuous, supported and coordinated with services; metal-frame and reflective arrangements have additional project rules.

cad.pattern: Layered roof or ceiling fields interrupted by framing and services
cad.placement: At the upper conditioned-space boundary
cad.opening: Detailed around roof lights, flues, ducts, fans and access hatches
cad.load: Insulation supported by framing, lining or proprietary restraints

objects.name: pitched-roof horizontal-ceiling insulation assembly
objects.definition: An upper-envelope arrangement in which the primary insulation follows a horizontal ceiling below a pitched roof, usually leaving a separate roof space above.

cad.pattern: Repeated insulation units across ceiling framing bays
cad.placement: On or above the horizontal ceiling lining
cad.opening: Cut or cleared only for documented services and access
cad.load: Non-structural insulation supported by ceiling system

notes: The roof space above is a separate void and may have its own ventilation objects.

objects.name: cathedral or skillion roof insulation assembly
objects.definition: A sloping upper-envelope build-up where ceiling and roof planes are close together and insulation, ventilation gaps, membranes and framing must be coordinated within a limited depth.
functions: Preserve required ventilation or drainage gaps

cad.pattern: Sloping layered fields between or across roof framing
cad.placement: Between roof cladding and sloping internal ceiling
cad.opening: Maintains documented paths around roof lights, flues and ducts
cad.load: Insulation supported by framing, battens, lining or proprietary fasteners

notes: A narrow unventilated cavity must not be labelled a compliant roof space merely because it is empty.

objects.name: external wall thermal assembly
objects.definition: The external-wall build-up as a thermal element, including structure, cavity or continuous insulation, membranes, cladding, lining, openings and junctions at floors, ceilings and adjoining walls.
functions: Limit heat transfer through external walls
Keep insulation continuous at openings and junctions

cad.pattern: Layered wall fields with repeated framing and explicit opening returns
cad.placement: At conditioned-space external walls
cad.opening: Wraps insulation and membranes around doors, windows and services
cad.load: Thermal layers non-structural; support comes from wall assembly

objects.name: framed-wall cavity insulation assembly
objects.definition: Insulation cut or selected to fill nominated bays between wall studs and noggings while remaining fitted around services and openings without unintended gaps or compression.
functions: Fit around wall services and bracing
Connect to perimeter and opening insulation

cad.pattern: One or more fitted insulation pieces per framing bay
cad.placement: Between studs, plates and noggings
cad.opening: Cut closely around services and opening framing
cad.load: Non-structural infill retained by fit or supports

notes: Do not stretch one batt through a nogging or stud; each interrupted bay needs explicit pieces.

objects.name: continuous wall insulation assembly
objects.definition: A substantially uninterrupted insulation layer installed across the face of wall framing or masonry, with separately detailed fixings, joints, openings and cladding or lining supports.
functions: Connect wall insulation across framing members

cad.pattern: Continuous board or roll courses across the wall face
cad.placement: Inside or outside structural wall framing as selected
cad.opening: Cut and returned around doors, windows and penetrations
cad.load: Non-structural layer held by documented fasteners and supports

notes: Fasteners and brackets penetrating the layer remain explicit because they affect support and thermal performance.

objects.name: masonry cavity insulation assembly
objects.definition: Insulation positioned within a masonry cavity or against one leaf while preserving the nominated drainage, tie, flashing, weephole and clear-cavity functions of the wall.
functions: Coordinate board joints or cavity fill around openings

cad.pattern: Boards, batts or fill volumes between masonry leaves or frame and veneer
cad.placement: Within the documented wall cavity
cad.opening: Continues around opening reveals without blocking drainage
cad.load: Non-structural insulation restrained by clips, ties or cavity geometry

notes: Full-fill, partial-fill and blown retrofit systems are not interchangeable layouts.

objects.name: suspended floor insulation assembly
objects.definition: Insulation and its wind-wash facing, restraints or continuous layers installed within or across a suspended timber, steel or concrete floor at the thermal boundary.
functions: Limit heat flow through a suspended floor
Keep insulation in position against gravity and air movement

cad.pattern: Repeated infill between floor members or continuous layer below them
cad.placement: At underside or within suspended floor framing
cad.opening: Cut and restrained around pipes, ducts and supports
cad.load: Non-structural insulation carried by floor framing and restraints

objects.name: enclosed subfloor wall insulation assembly
objects.definition: An insulation layer installed to the walls enclosing a subfloor space when that wall, rather than or together with the suspended floor, forms part of the thermal boundary.
functions: Connect wall insulation to floor and ground interfaces

cad.pattern: Insulated perimeter wall fields around an enclosed subfloor
cad.placement: On internal or external face of subfloor enclosure walls
cad.opening: Stops around vents without obstructing their free area
cad.load: Non-structural insulation supported by wall construction

notes: Vent openings remain holes and fittings in the wall, not deleted insulation metadata.

objects.name: slab-on-ground insulation assembly
objects.definition: The coordinated insulation installed beneath and or around the perimeter of a concrete slab-on-ground, including board joints, edge protection and moisture and termite interfaces.
functions: Reduce heat transfer through slab and edge
Coordinate insulation with damp-proofing and termite inspection

cad.pattern: Horizontal boards below slab connected to vertical perimeter strips where selected
cad.placement: Beneath slab and against vertical slab edge
cad.opening: Cut tightly around services and structural thickenings
cad.load: Under-slab boards carry documented construction and slab loads

notes: The existing foundation catalogue retains the canonical slab-edge insulation object; this record coordinates the whole assembly.

objects.name: pliable building membrane system
objects.definition: A selected pliable sheet together with laps, tapes, patches, sleeves, fixings and terminations that performs documented water, air, vapour or reflective functions in a roof, wall or floor assembly.
functions: Connect membrane fields to openings and adjacent layers

ncc_references.relationship: External-wall membrane position and vapour permeance depend on the assembly and climate zone; product function cannot be inferred from foil appearance.

cad.pattern: Overlapping sheet courses with sealed joints and local patches
cad.placement: At the documented face within roof, wall or floor build-up
cad.start: Lowest drained or first sheet edge
cad.opening: Cut, turned and taped around openings and penetrations
cad.load: Non-structural membrane supported by framing, substrate or battens

notes: Water, air, vapour and reflective classifications are independent attributes; one product can perform several without making the terms synonyms.

objects.name: residential building air-sealing system
objects.definition: The connected internal linings, membranes, compressible seals, foams, caulking, dampers and opening seals that limit unintended air leakage through the conditioned-space boundary.
functions: Limit unintended air infiltration and exfiltration
Preserve deliberate ventilation and combustion-air openings

ncc_references.relationship: Physical seals are required at nominated envelope openings, junctions, fans, coolers and flues while safety ventilation openings remain available.

cad.pattern: Continuous air-control layer with linear and discrete seals at every interruption
cad.placement: At the conditioned-space boundary
cad.opening: Connects to seals and operable dampers at openings
cad.load: Non-structural seals supported by envelope components

notes: Airtightness is a measured assembly property, not a material that can be painted onto the model.

objects.name: roof-space ventilation system
objects.definition: A coordinated roof-space air path using distributed low-level, high-level or opposing-end openings, their vents, screens, flashings and insulation baffles to exchange air with outdoors.
functions: Provide deliberate outdoor-air exchange above insulation
Keep insulation and debris clear of required free area

ncc_references.relationship: Climate-zone, pitch, location and free-open-area rules select and size physical roof-space openings; the airflow itself is not a solid object.

cad.pattern: Distributed inlet and outlet fittings connected by an unobstructed roof-space void
cad.placement: At eaves, ridge, gables or roof penetrations as designed
cad.opening: Each vent retains net free area after mesh and fittings
cad.load: Vents supported by soffit, fascia, wall or roof construction

notes: Free open area is an attribute of the finished opening, not its nominal grille outline.

objects.name: subfloor ventilation system
objects.definition: A set of external and internal wall openings, grilles or brick vents arranged to provide unobstructed cross-ventilation through the space below a suspended floor.
functions: Coordinate ground moisture control with wall openings

ncc_references.relationship: Requires distributed external and internal openings and unobstructed cross-flow below suspended floors, with ground membrane and damp-site alternatives kept explicit.

cad.pattern: Distributed external openings aligned through internal subfloor walls
cad.placement: In perimeter and internal walls below suspended floors
cad.opening: Openings through double leaves align as one passage
cad.load: Openings trimmed or lintelled by host wall where required

notes: The cross-flow path is a relationship between voids and openings, not a pipe drawn through the subfloor.

objects.name: room exhaust and make-up-air system
objects.definition: A mechanical source-exhaust arrangement comprising a room intake or fan, duct or shaft, outdoor terminal, controls and a deliberate path for replacement air.
functions: Remove moisture and pollutants to outdoors
Provide replacement air to the exhausted room
Prevent reverse leakage when the fan is off

ncc_references.relationship: Domestic exhaust must discharge outdoors through physical duct or shaft routes, may need controls and make-up air, and requires a sealing device at nominated envelope conditions.

cad.pattern: Fan and intake connected by duct or shaft to an outdoor terminal, with a separate make-up-air path
cad.placement: From kitchen, bathroom, sanitary compartment, laundry or venting dryer to outdoors
cad.opening: Penetrates linings and envelope with coordinated seals
cad.load: Equipment and ducts supported independently by building structure

notes: A fan dumping into a roof space is not represented as a completed outdoor-discharge system.

objects.name: building thermal insulation product
objects.definition: A manufactured or installed product whose documented role is to resist heat flow in a building element, with declared form, material, dimensions and thermal properties.
functions: Form part of a documented thermal barrier
Provide a selectable product identity for placement
materials: fibrous, cellular, foamed, reflective or composite insulation

cad.pattern: Selected product units or continuous installed field
cad.placement: Within the nominated thermal envelope assembly
cad.opening: Fitted or cut around documented interruptions
cad.load: Non-structural unless the selected composite product states otherwise

notes: R-value is an attribute of a declared product or complete construction, not a separate material object.

objects.name: bulk thermal insulation
objects.definition: Insulation that obtains much of its thermal resistance from thickness and trapped gas within a fibrous, cellular, granular or foamed material rather than from a reflective airspace alone.
functions: Provide thermal resistance through material thickness
Fill or cover selected envelope fields

cad.pattern: Discrete units, rolls, fill volumes or sprayed fields
cad.placement: Between or across envelope framing
cad.opening: Cut or placed closely around allowed services
cad.load: Non-structural insulation retained by geometry or supports

objects.name: reflective insulation
objects.definition: A low-emittance surface or surfaces installed facing a documented airspace so the combined layer-and-airspace arrangement contributes thermal resistance.
functions: Reduce radiant heat transfer across an airspace
Contribute to a documented system R-value
Combine with other membrane control functions where classified

cad.pattern: Continuous reflective sheet adjacent to explicit airspace volume
cad.placement: At selected roof, wall or floor layer
cad.opening: Closely fitted and taped around openings as documented
cad.load: Non-structural sheet supported by framing or substrate

notes: The reflective airspace is a separate geometric void; drawing foil directly against another layer must not receive an airspace R-value.

objects.name: thermal insulation batt
objects.definition: A pre-cut semi-rigid or resilient rectangular insulation unit sized for repeated placement between framing members or, for selected products, across them.

cad.pattern: Repeated rectangular units fitted to framing bays
cad.placement: Between or across framing as product permits
cad.opening: Cut into separate fitted pieces around services and framing
cad.load: Non-structural infill

objects.name: thermal insulation blanket or roll
objects.definition: A flexible insulation product supplied in a continuous roll or long blanket and cut to length across roof, ceiling, wall or floor supports.
functions: Reduce the number of transverse joints
Combine insulation with a facing where manufactured as a composite

cad.pattern: Continuous strips unrolled across or between supports
cad.placement: At selected roof, ceiling, wall or floor layer
cad.opening: Cut and sealed or fitted around penetrations
cad.load: Non-structural blanket supported by framing or cladding system

notes: Roof blanket is an application-specific roll, not a synonym for every insulation roll.

objects.name: loose-fill thermal insulation
objects.definition: Granular, nodular or fibrous insulation placed as loose material to a documented installed depth and density over a horizontal surface or within an approved contained cavity.
functions: Provide thermal resistance at documented settled depth

cad.pattern: Continuous granular or fibrous volume with variable top surface
cad.placement: Over horizontal ceilings or in approved contained spaces
cad.opening: Excluded or retained around services according to product system
cad.load: Non-structural loose material supported from below

notes: Nominal depth and settled installed depth remain separate attributes.

objects.name: blown-in insulation layer
objects.definition: An installed field of fibrous insulation pneumatically blown into an open roof or ceiling area or injected into a documented enclosed cavity through access holes.
functions: Fill accessible or enclosed irregular volumes
Create a continuous installed insulation field
Support retrofit where product and host permit

cad.pattern: Continuous fill volume bounded by cavity or ceiling field
cad.placement: Within approved wall cavities or over ceilings
cad.opening: Injection openings and obstructions remain documented
cad.load: Non-structural fill contained by host construction

notes: Do not infer a fully filled cavity from the presence of one injection hole.

objects.name: rigid thermal insulation board
objects.definition: A dimensionally stable insulation panel cut and joined within or across an envelope assembly and held by fit, adhesive, fasteners, battens or the supported construction.
functions: Form cavity or continuous insulation fields
Support precise joints and opening returns

cad.pattern: Repeated rectangular panels with butt, rebated or taped joints
cad.placement: Within framing, cavities, below slabs, at soffits or continuously across structure
cad.opening: Cut closely and sealed or infilled around services
cad.load: Non-structural unless selected product has documented load role

objects.name: glass mineral-wool insulation
objects.definition: Fibrous insulation manufactured mainly from glass and binder, supplied in batts, rolls, blankets or loose blow-in form for selected building applications.
functions: Fit framing bays or continuous roll fields

cad.pattern: Material classification applied to batt, roll or blown geometry
cad.placement: As permitted by selected product
cad.opening: Uses the geometry of the selected form
cad.load: Non-structural insulation

notes: Material and product form remain separate classifications: glass mineral wool may be a batt, roll or blown layer.

objects.name: rock mineral-wool insulation
objects.definition: Fibrous insulation manufactured from molten rock or similar mineral feedstock and supplied as batts, blankets or boards for documented thermal, acoustic or fire-system applications.
functions: Contribute to documented acoustic or fire assemblies where included

cad.pattern: Material classification applied to batt, blanket or board geometry
cad.placement: As permitted by selected product and assembly
cad.opening: Uses selected product geometry
cad.load: Non-structural insulation

notes: Fire use depends on the complete tested assembly; mineral fibre appearance alone does not make a penetration firestop.

objects.name: polyester-fibre insulation
objects.definition: A resilient non-woven polyester-fibre insulation product supplied in batts or rolls for documented wall, ceiling, roof or floor applications.
functions: Offer a non-mineral fibrous product option

cad.pattern: Batt or roll units following selected product dimensions
cad.placement: Within or across framing as documented
cad.opening: Cut or fitted around allowed interruptions
cad.load: Non-structural fibrous insulation

objects.name: cellulose-fibre insulation
objects.definition: Loose or damp-sprayed fibrous insulation based mainly on processed cellulose and installed to a documented density, depth or cavity-fill procedure.
functions: Support retrofit installation where the host and system permit

cad.pattern: Filled field or cavity volume
cad.placement: Within approved ceiling, roof or wall application
cad.opening: Placed around services with documented clearances
cad.load: Non-structural fibrous fill

objects.name: expanded-polystyrene insulation board
objects.definition: A rigid cellular insulation board made from fused expanded-polystyrene beads and selected by grade, dimensions and documented building application.
functions: Form under-slab, wall or composite insulation fields
Allow board cutting and joint layout

cad.pattern: Repeated rigid panels with documented joint layout
cad.placement: At selected wall, floor, slab or roof position
cad.opening: Cut around penetrations and structural elements
cad.load: Carries only documented loads for selected grade

objects.name: extruded-polystyrene insulation board
objects.definition: A rigid closed-cell insulation board formed by extruding polystyrene and selected for documented wall, floor, slab-edge or below-slab conditions.
functions: Resist documented moisture and compressive exposure

cad.pattern: Repeated rigid boards with close joints
cad.placement: At documented slab, wall, roof or floor position
cad.opening: Cut around penetrations and structural elements
cad.load: Carries only documented loads for selected grade

objects.name: polyisocyanurate insulation board
objects.definition: A rigid closed-cell polyisocyanurate foam insulation board commonly manufactured with foil or other facings for selected roof, wall or floor systems.
functions: Provide high thermal resistance in a thin board
Integrate documented facings and sealed joints

cad.pattern: Repeated faced boards with close or taped joints
cad.placement: At selected roof, wall or floor layer
cad.opening: Cut and sealed around penetrations
cad.load: Non-structural unless part of documented composite system

objects.name: phenolic insulation board
objects.definition: A rigid thermoset phenolic foam insulation board, usually faced, cut for framing, cavity, soffit, wall or floor applications supported by its selected product system.
functions: Provide high thermal resistance in a thin board

cad.pattern: Repeated faced boards fitted within or across construction
cad.placement: At documented framing, cavity, soffit, floor or slab position
cad.opening: Cut, infilled and sealed around services
cad.load: Non-structural unless selected composite states otherwise

notes: A proprietary brand name is not used as the canonical material family.

objects.name: sprayed foam insulation layer
objects.definition: A cellular insulation material mixed or dispensed on site and sprayed onto or into a compatible substrate or cavity where it expands or cures into a continuous adhered layer.
functions: Reduce local air movement where the documented system permits

cad.pattern: Irregular continuous cured layer following substrate
cad.placement: On or within approved building elements
cad.opening: Stops or is trimmed around services and required clearances
cad.load: Non-structural adhered insulation

notes: The small expanding-foam bead used to seal a joint is a separate air-seal object.

objects.name: foil-faced insulation board
objects.definition: A factory-made rigid insulation board with one or more bonded foil or low-emittance composite facings, whose core and faces retain separate thermal, vapour and surface attributes.
functions: Provide a reflective face when an airspace exists
Contribute documented air or vapour control at sealed joints

cad.pattern: Repeated faced panels with documented taped or butted joints
cad.placement: At selected envelope layer
cad.opening: Cut and sealed around penetrations
cad.load: Non-structural board supported by system fixings

notes: A foil face touching another layer has no reflective airspace merely because the face is shiny.

objects.name: insulated plasterboard composite
objects.definition: A factory-laminated panel combining an internal plasterboard lining with a rigid insulation backing for direct or framed installation as one selected product.
functions: Provide continuous internal insulation where documented

cad.pattern: Repeated composite lining panels with staggered or scheduled joints
cad.placement: On internal face of walls or ceilings as selected
cad.opening: Cut and returned at openings with product-compatible details
cad.load: Non-structural lining and insulation composite

objects.name: ceiling insulation layer
objects.definition: The installed insulation field following a ceiling plane, including individual units, cuts, edge overlaps and intentional reductions or clearances recorded against the selected system.
functions: Connect to wall insulation at perimeter

cad.pattern: Continuous field assembled from repeated units or fill
cad.placement: On, between or across ceiling supports
cad.opening: Records each excluded, reduced or infilled service area
cad.load: Non-structural insulation supported by ceiling construction

objects.name: wall cavity insulation layer
objects.definition: The complete insulation field occupying nominated wall cavities or framing bays, represented independently from the material and unit form used to create it.

cad.pattern: Connected field comprising individual bay infill pieces
cad.placement: Within external-wall framing or approved masonry cavity
cad.opening: Stops and returns around openings and services
cad.load: Non-structural insulation

objects.name: continuous insulation layer
objects.definition: An insulation field installed with substantial continuity across structural framing members to reduce repeating heat-flow paths through those members.
functions: Provide an explicit continuous layer for calculations and detailing

cad.pattern: Continuous sheet, board or blanket field across framing lines
cad.placement: Above, below, inside or outside framing as selected
cad.opening: Cut and returned or infilled at all openings
cad.load: Non-structural layer held by documented fixings

notes: Fasteners and necessary openings do not erase the concept, but their extent must remain available to the thermal model.

objects.name: stacked insulation layers
objects.definition: Two or more insulation layers placed directly over one another with controlled orientation and joint staggering so an upper layer can cover framing or joints in the layer below.
functions: Combine thermal resistance of multiple layers
Provide an explicit layer order and joint pattern

cad.pattern: Superimposed insulation fields with separate unit grids
cad.placement: Across ceiling or roof framing as selected
cad.opening: Each layer retains separate cuts and clearances
cad.load: Non-structural layers supported from below

notes: Layer order, compression and crossing direction must be retained instead of summing nominal R-values blindly.

objects.name: underfloor insulation layer
objects.definition: The installed insulation field fitted between or across suspended-floor members and held against gravity, wind-wash and service interruptions by its product facing or separate restraints.
functions: Record individual pieces and continuous fields

cad.pattern: Repeated infill pieces or continuous boards below floor framing
cad.placement: Between or beneath suspended-floor members
cad.opening: Cut and retained around services and supports
cad.load: Non-structural insulation retained against gravity

objects.name: subfloor wall insulation layer
objects.definition: The installed insulation field on or within a wall enclosing a subfloor space, stopped and detailed around ventilation openings, access points and the floor and ground junctions.
functions: Connect the floor boundary to the perimeter wall

cad.pattern: Continuous or bay insulation around subfloor perimeter walls
cad.placement: On or within walls enclosing an underfloor space
cad.opening: Trimmed around every ventilation and access opening
cad.load: Non-structural insulation supported by wall

objects.name: under-slab insulation board
objects.definition: A load-compatible rigid insulation board installed below a concrete slab-on-ground over prepared support and coordinated with membranes, joints, thickenings and service penetrations.
functions: Reduce heat flow through the slab field
Maintain a continuous under-slab insulation layer
Transfer documented construction loads to the base
materials: phenolic, XPS, EPS or other approved rigid board

cad.pattern: Repeated boards over prepared base below slab
cad.placement: Between prepared ground layers and concrete slab
cad.opening: Cut around pipes, piles, beams and thickenings
cad.load: Carries documented slab and construction loads through selected grade

objects.name: soffit insulation board
objects.definition: A rigid or faced insulation board mechanically fixed to the underside of a concrete slab, floor or roof soffit as a visible or lined continuous thermal layer.
functions: Coordinate board fixings, joints and edge terminations

cad.pattern: Repeated boards fixed to soffit with explicit anchor grid
cad.placement: Below suspended slab, floor or roof substrate
cad.opening: Cut and terminated around columns, pipes and fixtures
cad.load: Self-weight carried by documented anchors into structure

objects.name: insulation infill piece
objects.definition: A deliberately cut piece of compatible insulation used to close the residual space beside framing, services, off-grid bays or board edges where a full standard unit does not fit.
functions: Continue the thermal layer around irregular geometry
materials: compatible batt, board or fibrous insulation

cad.pattern: Irregular cut piece at residual gap
cad.placement: Between full insulation units and host geometry
cad.opening: Fitted around documented obstruction
cad.load: Non-structural infill retained by fit or compatible seal

notes: A model should preserve the parent product so an offcut does not become an unclassified generic filler.

objects.name: window and door perimeter insulation
objects.definition: Compressible or cut insulation fitted in the available gap between a window or door assembly and adjoining wall framing to continue the wall thermal layer without preventing required movement or drainage.
functions: Connect wall insulation to frame perimeter
Allow documented movement and separate air and water seals

cad.pattern: Continuous or segmented strip around opening perimeter
cad.placement: Between product frame and structural rough opening
cad.opening: Occupies perimeter gap without blocking drainage or movement
cad.load: Non-structural insulation; packers carry frame loads

objects.name: insulation support netting
objects.definition: A flexible mesh or net fixed beneath or behind bulk insulation to stop it sagging or falling from a floor, wall, ceiling or roof framing bay.
functions: Distribute support over a broad area
Keep installed thickness and position visible

cad.pattern: Continuous mesh spanning framing bays with fixed edges
cad.placement: Below or behind bulk insulation
cad.opening: Cut and refixed around penetrations
cad.load: Carries insulation self-weight only as documented

objects.name: insulation support strap
objects.definition: A narrow flexible strip fixed across framing members at repeated intervals to retain underfloor, wall or overhead insulation against sagging or falling.
functions: Create a visible support spacing pattern

cad.pattern: Repeated narrow strips crossing framing bays
cad.placement: Under insulation between floor or roof framing
cad.opening: Rerouted or separately fixed around services
cad.load: Carries local insulation self-weight

objects.name: insulation retaining wire
objects.definition: A wire run or spring wire fitted across a framing bay to hold an insulation batt or blanket in its intended position.

cad.pattern: Repeated wire lines across insulation bays
cad.placement: Across framing bay on exposed side of insulation
cad.opening: Additional wires placed around interruptions
cad.load: Carries local insulation self-weight

objects.name: insulation retaining clip or hanger
objects.definition: A discrete clip, pin, hanger or retainer fixed to framing or substrate to support insulation boards, batts or blankets at documented points.
functions: Locate boards or batts before finishes

cad.pattern: Repeated discrete fixing grid
cad.placement: Through or beside insulation into host
cad.opening: Fixings offset from joints and services as scheduled
cad.load: Transfers insulation self-weight and documented wind actions

objects.name: underfloor insulation wind-wash facing
objects.definition: A factory-applied or separate air-resistant facing on exposed underfloor insulation that limits outdoor air moving through or across the fibrous insulation.
functions: Limit wind washing of fibrous insulation

cad.pattern: Thin face layer following underside of insulation units
cad.placement: On subfloor-exposed face of underfloor insulation
cad.opening: Cut and retained around services
cad.load: Non-structural facing bonded to or supported with insulation

objects.name: reflective insulation airspace
objects.definition: A documented unfilled air volume adjoining a low-emittance insulation face and bounded by building layers so the combined arrangement can provide reflective thermal resistance.
functions: Provide the airspace required by reflective insulation
Separate the reflective face from adjacent solid layers
Record depth, direction and ventilation condition

cad.pattern: Continuous void bounded by reflective surface and opposing layer
cad.placement: Immediately adjacent to selected reflective insulation face
cad.opening: Interrupted by framing, fixings and closures as modelled
cad.load: Void; bounding construction carries loads

notes: Airspace geometry is drawable; its R-value remains calculated metadata based on the complete condition.

objects.name: pliable building membrane
objects.definition: A flexible sheet product installed as a building underlay or wrap and classified separately for water, air, vapour, duty, emittance and flammability functions.
functions: Provide one or more documented control-layer functions
Span or cover building framing and substrates
Receive laps, tapes, patches and fixings

cad.pattern: Overlapping flexible sheet courses
cad.placement: At selected roof, wall or floor layer
cad.opening: Cut, folded and taped at openings and penetrations
cad.load: Non-structural sheet supported by framing, substrate or battens

notes: Roof sarking and external wall weather-barrier roles already have discipline-specific canonical records; this object provides the shared product class.

objects.name: vapour-control membrane
objects.definition: A pliable membrane selected and positioned for its documented resistance or openness to water-vapour diffusion through a building assembly.
functions: Provide a classified material layer for condensation assessment

cad.pattern: Continuous membrane field at selected side of primary insulation
cad.placement: Within wall, roof or floor build-up as designed
cad.opening: Sealed at openings and penetrations where the system requires
cad.load: Non-structural control layer

notes: The canonical name covers both vapour-resistant and vapour-open products; their classifications must not be lost.

objects.name: vapour-barrier membrane
objects.definition: A vapour-control membrane with low documented vapour permeance, installed only where the climate, layer order and condensation strategy support restricting diffusion.
functions: Form part of a climate-specific vapour-control strategy

cad.pattern: Continuous low-permeance membrane field
cad.placement: At the designed side of insulation for the selected climate and assembly
cad.opening: Sealed around penetrations according to strategy
cad.load: Non-structural membrane

notes: Using vapour barrier as a generic name for every wall wrap is unsafe.

objects.name: vapour-permeable membrane
objects.definition: A vapour-control membrane with documented vapour openness that can permit outward or inward drying while performing any separately classified water or air-control functions.
functions: Support drying of selected wall or roof layers
Provide other documented wrap functions without trapping vapour

cad.pattern: Continuous vapour-open membrane field
cad.placement: At documented side of insulation, commonly exterior in cooler climate wall paths
cad.opening: Taped and flashed around openings
cad.load: Non-structural membrane

notes: Breathable is held as loose language because it may refer to vapour diffusion, air leakage or both.

objects.name: air-barrier membrane
objects.definition: A membrane classified and installed to resist unintended airflow through the envelope, with sealed laps, edges and penetrations forming part of a continuous air-control layer.
functions: Limit air leakage through membrane fields
Connect air seals at joints and openings

objects.name: reflective foil laminate membrane

cad.opening: Follows support and transition geometry

objects.name: pliable membrane penetration patch

Provide a shaped transition from sheet to service

objects.name: pliable membrane fastener

cad.opening: Fixing puncture covered or sealed where system requires
cad.load: Retains membrane

objects.name: membrane cap washer

objects.name: pliable membrane sealant adhesive
objects.definition: A compatible cartridge, bead or liquid adhesive used to bond and seal a pliable membrane to concrete, masonry, timber, metal, frames or another approved substrate at edges and transitions.

objects.name: metal roof thermal-break strip

objects.name: metal wall-frame thermal-break strip

objects.name: metal suspended-floor thermal-break layer

objects.name: thermal isolation pad

objects.name: thermally broken support bracket

objects.name: continuous-insulation fastener

objects.name: thermal spacer batten

objects.name: expanding foam air seal

materials: sleeve or cavity liner where detailed

cad.pattern: One aligned passage through two leaves per vent location
cad.placement: Across double-leaf external or internal subfloor wall
cad.opening: Passes through outer leaf, cavity and inner leaf
cad.load: Masonry supported around openings

objects.name: subfloor brick vent
objects.definition: A perforated masonry-sized metal, terracotta, concrete or polymer vent unit built into a subfloor wall in place of one or more masonry units.
functions: Provide a durable subfloor wall vent
Screen and finish the ventilation opening
not_synonyms: wall vent grille for framed wall automatically

cad.pattern: Discrete vent units coordinated to masonry courses
cad.placement: Built into subfloor masonry wall
cad.opening: Replaces one or more wall units
cad.load: Surrounding masonry and lintel support wall loads

objects.name: subfloor ventilation grille
objects.definition: A framed louvred, perforated or bar grille fixed over a subfloor wall opening to protect and finish it while preserving documented free open area.
functions: Provide removable maintenance access where designed

cad.pattern: Discrete grilles over wall openings
cad.placement: On external or internal face of subfloor wall vent
cad.opening: Covers but does not block wall opening
cad.load: Supported by wall fixings

objects.name: subfloor ground vapour membrane
objects.definition: An impervious sheet laid over exposed ground beneath a suspended floor, with lapped or sealed joints and perimeter treatment, to reduce water vapour entering the subfloor space from soil.
functions: Work with subfloor ventilation and drainage

ncc_references.relationship: An impervious ground membrane is a physical damp-subfloor alternative and changes the ventilation-opening calculation without becoming an under-slab membrane.

cad.pattern: Overlapping sheets covering accessible subfloor ground
cad.placement: On prepared soil below suspended floor
cad.opening: Cut and sealed or turned around piers, stumps and services
cad.load: Non-structural sheet supported by ground

notes: The existing foundation membrane remains the canonical under-slab object; this record is for an exposed subfloor ground-cover role.

objects.name: ceiling-mounted room exhaust fan
objects.definition: A fan assembly mounted through a ceiling lining with a room-side grille or diffuser and a discharge spigot connected to ducting or a permitted outdoor path.
functions: Connect ceiling intake to exhaust duct
Support controls and a sealing damper

cad.pattern: One or more ceiling fan fixtures per served room
cad.placement: Through ceiling lining with duct outlet above
cad.opening: Occupies ceiling cut-out and seals at lining
cad.load: Supported by ceiling frame or approved clips

notes: Presence of a fan does not prove outdoor discharge; the duct and terminal must be connected explicitly.

objects.name: wall-mounted room exhaust fan
objects.definition: A fan assembly mounted through or on a wall with a room-side intake and an outdoor terminal, duct sleeve or connected duct on the discharge side.
functions: Extract room air through a wall

cad.pattern: One fan assembly through external wall
cad.placement: In wall opening between room and outdoors
cad.opening: Penetrates wall and control layers
cad.load: Supported by wall framing or sleeve

objects.name: inline exhaust duct fan
objects.definition: A fan body installed within a duct run away from the room intake, connected to upstream and downstream ducts and separately supported for service access.
functions: Serve one or more compatible intake points as designed

cad.pattern: One fan inserted between duct segments
cad.placement: In accessible ceiling, wall or service space
cad.opening: Forms part of continuous duct run
cad.load: Independently supported by bracket or straps

objects.name: ducted kitchen rangehood exhaust assembly
objects.definition: A kitchen hood containing filters, fan or remote-fan connection, capture canopy, duct spigot and controls, connected by ductwork to an outdoor discharge terminal.
functions: Provide accessible grease filtration and controls

ncc_references.relationship: Kitchen and rangehood exhaust must discharge to outdoor air rather than terminate in the roof space.

cad.pattern: Canopy over cooking appliance connected to outdoor duct route
cad.placement: Above or behind cooking appliance
cad.opening: Duct penetrates cabinetry, ceiling, wall or roof with seals
cad.load: Hood and duct independently supported

objects.name: venting clothes-dryer exhaust assembly
objects.definition: A connection, duct and outdoor terminal carrying warm moist exhaust from a venting clothes dryer directly to outdoor air.
functions: Connect appliance outlet to a compatible duct route
Limit lint accumulation through accessible components

ncc_references.relationship: A venting clothes dryer requires a physical duct or shaft route to outdoor air; condensing dryers are a different appliance arrangement.

cad.pattern: Continuous appliance exhaust route to outdoors
cad.placement: From dryer outlet through laundry wall, floor or ceiling to external terminal
cad.opening: Penetrates cabinetry and envelope with accessible connections
cad.load: Duct independently clipped or supported

objects.name: domestic exhaust duct
objects.definition: A rigid or flexible round or rectangular duct conveying room or appliance exhaust from an intake, hood or fan to an outdoor terminal or shaft connection.
functions: Keep moisture and contaminants out of concealed building spaces
Connect fans, fittings and outdoor terminals

cad.pattern: Continuous routed run between equipment and outdoor terminal
cad.placement: Within ceiling, wall, floor or service space
cad.opening: Passes through construction with sleeves and seals
cad.load: Supported by clips, straps or brackets

notes: Flexible and rigid duct forms should become subtypes in the dedicated mechanical-services slice.

objects.name: domestic exhaust duct fitting
objects.definition: A bend, reducer, adaptor, branch, coupler, spigot or clamp that changes direction, size or connection within a domestic exhaust duct route.

cad.pattern: Discrete fitting between duct or equipment segments
cad.placement: At each route change or connection
cad.opening: Maintains continuous air passage
cad.load: Supported with adjacent duct or separate bracket

objects.name: domestic outdoor exhaust terminal
objects.definition: A weather-protected wall or roof cowl, grille, hood or shutter at the outdoor end of a domestic exhaust duct or shaft.
functions: Protect the duct from weather and pests
Restrict reverse flow with a damper or shutters where included

cad.pattern: One terminal at each independent outdoor exhaust route
cad.placement: Through external wall or roof covering
cad.opening: Penetrates envelope with flashing and air seal
cad.load: Supported by wall, roof or duct system

objects.name: exhaust-fan run-on timer
objects.definition: An electrical control that keeps an exhaust fan operating for a preset period after the initiating light switch, occupancy control or manual switch is turned off.
functions: Extend exhaust operation after room use
Provide an adjustable or fixed run-on period

ncc_references.relationship: A physical run-on timer is part of the nominated non-continuous bathroom or sanitary-compartment exhaust arrangement.

cad.pattern: One control module per fan or control circuit
cad.placement: Within fan, wall box, switchboard or accessible control location
cad.opening: Requires enclosure or wall-box space
cad.load: Supported by electrical enclosure or fan housing

objects.name: exhaust-fan light-switch interlock
objects.definition: A physical switch, relay or wiring-control arrangement that starts the room exhaust fan when the associated room light is switched on.
functions: Link fan operation to room light use

ncc_references.relationship: A light-switch interlock physically initiates nominated non-continuous exhaust systems where natural ventilation is not available.

cad.pattern: One switch or relay relationship connecting room light and fan
cad.placement: At wall switch, fan module or electrical enclosure
cad.opening: Occupies wall box or enclosure
cad.load: Supported by electrical mounting system

notes: The control relationship belongs in the graph; the switch or relay is the physical object.

objects.name: room make-up-air opening
objects.definition: A deliberate opening from an adjacent room or outdoor-air path that supplies replacement air to a room while its exhaust system operates.
functions: Connect adjacent spaces through a measured free area

ncc_references.relationship: A physical opening or AS 1668.2 path supplies make-up air to specified exhausted rooms that lack qualifying natural ventilation.

cad.pattern: One or more openings connecting exhausted room to replacement-air source
cad.placement: At door, wall, grille or duct boundary
cad.opening: Creates measured free passage through boundary
cad.load: Host door or wall frames opening

notes: Make-up air is deliberate geometry; an assumed leakage rate is not substituted for the opening.

objects.name: door undercut make-up-air opening
objects.definition: The clear gap between the bottom of an internal door leaf and the finished floor or threshold, deliberately sized to transfer make-up air when the door is closed.
functions: Transfer replacement air below a closed door
Avoid a separate wall grille where suitable
materials: air gap bounded by door leaf, jambs and floor

cad.pattern: Continuous rectangular gap below door leaf
cad.placement: Between closed internal door bottom and finished floor
cad.opening: Remains open when door is closed
cad.load: Void; door and frame carry loads

notes: This opening conflicts with a door-bottom air seal; the tool must resolve which regulatory and performance role applies to that door.

objects.name: room transfer-air grille
objects.definition: A framed louvred, perforated or baffled grille installed through a wall or door to permit make-up or transfer air between rooms while providing a finished opening.

cad.pattern: One or more framed grilles through room boundary
cad.placement: Low or designed level in internal wall or door
cad.opening: Occupies cut-out in door or wall
cad.load: Supported by grille frame and host
